sources.name: South Lhonak rapid-retreat and calving study
source_locators: Results and conclusions report 49.6 +/- 7.1 metres of glacier-front retreat immediately before the October 2023 event.
The reviewed full text identifies seven large calving events since 2017.
The authors interpret calving, moraine change, intermittent rainfall and breach as a combined event sequence rather than calving as a universal sole trigger.

sources.name: South Lhonak event-sequence reconstruction
sources.publisher: PubMed Central indexed primary observational study
source_locators: Discussion and Figure 5 report more than 100 metres of retreat and approximately 7 million cubic metres of calved ice.
The reconstruction separately reports approximately 38.31 million cubic metres of landslide debris and combined displacement waves.
Landslide volume is retained as competing-event context and is not counted as calved-ice volume.

sources.name: Sikkim Flash Flood Situation Report, 29 October 2023
sources.publisher: India Ministry of Home Affairs, Disaster Management Division
source_locators: The official annex identifies the South Lhonak glacial-lake outburst as the primary reason for the sudden Teesta River surge while noting that the exact cause was still under investigation.
The report records 88,400 people affected across four districts and 100 villages or wards.
The report records 42 confirmed deaths in Sikkim, 77 missing people, 2,002 damaged houses and 33 damaged bridges as of 29 October 2023.

metric_contract.unit: metres of front retreat, cubic metres of calved ice, repeated-event count and event-bounded downstream burden
metric_contract.geography: South Lhonak Glacier and glacial lake with the downstream Teesta River impact area in Sikkim, India
metric_contract.assessment_period: seven documented large calving events from 2017 through the October 2023 lake-outburst sequence and official 29 October 2023 impact tally
metric_contract.boundary: The receipt is event-bounded. It does not generalize one glacier to global calving frequency, count landslide debris as calved ice, or assert that calving alone caused the flood.

uncertainty: Front retreat and calved volume are study estimates with stated or study-specific remote-sensing uncertainty. The event reconstruction also identifies a much larger lateral-moraine landslide and displacement waves, and an independent trigger analysis emphasizes landslide processes; calving is therefore retained as one measured part of a compound event, not the sole cause. Official impacts are provisional as of 29 October 2023 and include the downstream GLOF disaster boundary, not impacts attributable exclusively to the calved-ice volume. No global frequency or global affected-area inference is made.
